close_reason: decision record captured; dual-constructor design (fail-open/fail-closed) is intentional and documented
description: from_cert and From<&Certificate> silently set name_constraints=None if the NameConstraints extension is malformed (lines 279-316). TryFrom<Certificate> propagates the der::Error to the caller (lines 318-342). A contributor may reasonably suggest collapsing these to always-fail or always-ignore. The split is intentional: embedded/offline callers using pre-vetted trust stores prefer not to fail on a parse quirk in an anchor cert they already trust; strict PKI callers (TLS, enterprise) need hard rejection of unparseable critical extensions per RFC 5280 §4.2. The doc comment on from_cert explicitly calls this out and points to try_from. Do not collapse these constructors.
title: TrustAnchor has dual constructors: from_cert/From fail-open on NC parse error, TryFrom fail-closed — this split is intentional
